title: Profiling low-mRNA content cells in complex human tissues using BD Rhapsody single-cell analysis
author: Scheiber, Trebo, et al.
materials: BD Horizon Dri Tumor and Tissue Dissociation Reagent

steps.title: Prepare reagents and buffers
steps.instruction: Prepare all required reagents and buffers as listed in the key resources table, thawing, vortexing and briefly centrifuging frozen stocks, and keep them on ice unless otherwise noted.

substeps.instruction: Prostate dissociation mix: DNase I 75 U/mL (20 µL), Collagenase Type V 2 % (1 mL), Dispase II 2.5 U/mL (1 mL), DMEM high glucose + 1 % L‑glutamine‑penicillin‑streptomycin (100 U/mL) – make 8 mL fresh, sterile‑filter, do not store.
Working buffer: BSA 10 % (10 mL) in DPBS, EDTA 1 % (5.88 mL) in DPBS – make 84.12 mL, sterile‑filter, store at 4 °C up to 1 week.
Erythrocyte lysis buffer: dilute 10× BD Pharm Lyse with ddH₂O to 1× (prepare fresh, do not store).
Calcein AM: dissolve in 503 µL DMSO, store at –20 °C up to 6 months.
80 % ethyl alcohol: add 2 mL nuclease‑free water to 8 mL absolute ethanol, store at RT up to 24 h.

steps.title: Dissociate prostate tissue
steps.instruction: Generate a single‑cell suspension from prostate biopsies using enzymatic digestion and mechanical mincing.

substeps.instruction: Use 10 mL prostate dissociation mix per sample.
Rinse a 0.8 cm biopsy in 5 mL cold DPBS, drain, and place in a new petri dish.
Add 5 mL freshly prepared dissociation mix, cut tissue into pieces <1 mm with sterile scissors or scalpel.
Pipette up/down, transfer the suspension to a 50 mL Falcon tube, wash the petri dish with another 5 mL dissociation mix and add to the tube.
Incubate tube in a pre‑heated water bath at 37 °C for 45 min, gently shaking every 5 min.
Stop digestion by adding 5 mL working buffer.
Strain through a 100 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube; rinse the original tube twice with 5 mL working buffer and repeat the filtration.
Centrifuge at 4 °C, 300 × g for 5 min.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL BD Sample Buffer (or 1 mL BD Stain Buffer if Sample Tag labeling is planned).
Optional: perform FACS enrichment before the resuspension.

steps.title: Dissociate lung tissue
steps.instruction: Generate a single‑cell suspension from lung lobectomy pieces using BD Horizon Dri Tumor and Tissue Dissociation Reagent (TTDR) and gentleMACS.

substeps.instruction: Prepare working buffer and BD Pharm Lyse lysing buffer as above.
Dissolve lyophilized TTDR with 5 mL warm HBSS; incubate at 37 °C ≤30 min (wear gloves, glasses, coat).
Add 5 mL HBSS to a gentleMACS C tube, weigh 0.3–1 g tissue, transfer with forceps, cut into small pieces.
Combine 5 mL TTDR with 5 mL HBSS in the C tube.
Run gentleMACS program h_tumor_01, then incubate 37 °C 15 min at 150 rpm.
Repeat program h_tumor_02, then finish with program h_tumor_03.
Strain through a 100 µm cell strainer into a 50 mL tube; use a 5 mL syringe plunger to press remaining tissue.
Rinse the C tube twice with 5 mL working buffer, combine rinses, fill tube to 45 mL with working buffer.
Centrifuge at 10 °C, 300 × g for 10 min.
Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 2–3 mL erythrocyte lysis buffer, incubate in the dark at 20 °C for 10 min.
Add 20–40 mL cold HBSS, centrifuge 4 °C, 300 × g for 8 min.
Aspirate supernatant, add 1 mL BD Sample Buffer, resuspend.
Pass the suspension through a 70 µm strainer three times (using fresh 50 mL tubes) to obtain ~4 mL final volume.
Optional: if Sample Tag labeling is performed, resuspend the final pellet in 1 mL BD Stain Buffer.

steps.title: Dissociate liver tissue
steps.instruction: Generate a single‑cell suspension from liver biopsies using TTDR and custom‑cut pipette tips.

substeps.instruction: Prepare working buffer and BD Pharm Lyse lysing buffer as above.
Dissolve TTDR with 5 mL warm HBSS; incubate at 37 °C ≤30 min.
Cut 5 mm off the narrow ends of sterile 1000 µL pipette tips with scissors.
Weigh 0.1–0.5 g liver tissue, add 2 mL cold HBSS in a petri dish, cut into pieces <1 mm.
Transfer tissue to a 15 mL Falcon tube using the cut pipette tips.
Add 2 mL warm TTDR, incubate 37 °C for 20 min at 150 rpm.
Place tube on ice to stop digestion, add 0.8 mL cold HBSS.
Pipette up/down vigorously with cut tips until solution turns cloudy/brown; repeat until tissue pieces sink.
Transfer supernatant to a new 15 mL tube on ice, add 1.6 mL cold HBSS to the remaining pieces and repeat extraction until no more cells are released (visual whitening of pieces).
Combine all supernatants, centrifuge 4 °C, 300 × g for 8 min.
Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 2–3 mL erythrocyte lysis buffer, incubate in the dark at 20 °C for 10 min.
Add 15 mL cold HBSS, centrifuge 4 °C, 300 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL BD Sample Buffer.
Filter through a 70 µm strainer into a fresh 50 mL tube, add 1 mL BD Sample Buffer to the original tube and filter again to reach ~2 mL total volume.
Optional: if Sample Tag labeling is performed, resuspend the final pellet in 1 mL BD Stain Buffer.

steps.title: Prime BD Rhapsody cartridge
steps.instruction: Prime the BD Rhapsody cartridge before loading cells and beads.

substeps.instruction: Place cartridge on the scanner, add a waste container and a 5 mL LoBind tube to the Express instrument drawer.
Set the BD Rhapsody P1200M pipette to “Prime/Treat” mode, move side slider to “0” and front slider to “Waste”.
Load 700 µL 100 % ethanol into the cartridge, followed by 700 µL air, then 700 µL Cartridge Wash Buffer 1.
Incubate 1 min, remove Wash Buffer 1 with 700 µL air.
Load another 700 µL Wash Buffer 1, incubate 10 min, then remove with 700 µL air.
Load 700 µL Cartridge Wash Buffer 2.
Seal the pipette tip airtight; use the primed cartridge within 4 h, store at 20 °C on the Express instrument.

steps.title: Load cells onto cartridge
steps.instruction: Load the prepared single‑cell suspension onto the primed cartridge and begin cell capture.

substeps.instruction: Remove Cartridge Wash Buffer 2 by aspirating 700 µL air.
Switch P1200M to “Cell Load” mode; gently resuspend cell suspension with a conventional pipette.
Press the pipette button three times: 1) aspirate 40 µL air, 2) aspirate 575 µL cell suspension, 3) dispense 615 µL into the cartridge.
Load 575 µL of the cell suspension onto the cartridge.
Place cartridge on the scanner, start a 20‑min incubation timer (extend the standard 15 min sedimentation by 5 min for small cells).
During incubation, prepare Enhanced Capture Beads (see next step).

steps.title: Prepare Enhanced Capture Beads
steps.instruction: Wash and resuspend the BD Rhapsody Enhanced Capture Beads before loading.

substeps.instruction: Place beads on a 1.5 mL magnetic rack, let settle 1 min.
Remove storage buffer while still on the magnet.
Transfer tube off the magnet, add 750 µL cold Sample Buffer, pipette up/down, keep on ice.
Never vortex the beads.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer
steps.instruction: Add DTT to the Lysis Buffer immediately before use.

substeps.instruction: Add 75 µL of 1 M DTT to the Lysis Buffer bottle, vortex 10 s, keep on ice.

steps.title: Load Enhanced Capture Beads
steps.instruction: Load the prepared beads onto the cartridge after cell capture.

substeps.instruction: Switch P1200M to “Prime/Treat” mode, load 700 µL air.
Resuspend beads gently with a conventional pipette.
Switch pipette to “Bead Load” mode, aspirate 630 µL bead suspension, load onto cartridge.
Set timer for 3 min, place cartridge on scanner.
After 3 min, start “Bead Load Scan”, then return cartridge to Express instrument.

steps.title: Wash beads in cartridge
steps.instruction: Perform two bead‑wash cycles to remove excess reagents.

substeps.instruction: Switch P1200M to “Wash” mode; press button three times: aspirate 720 µL Bead Wash Buffer, dispense 700 µL into cartridge, dispense 20 µL waste.
Aspirate 700 µL air to remove bead suspension.
Load 700 µL cold Sample Buffer.
Repeat the aspirate‑air‑load sequence once more.
Place cartridge on scanner, start “Bead Wash Scan”, then return to Express instrument.

steps.title: Lyse cells and retrieve beads
steps.instruction: Lyse captured cells, retrieve beads, and perform post‑lysis washes.

substeps.instruction: Switch P1200M to “Lysis” mode, move Express side slider to “Lysis" (front slider stays on “Waste”).
Load 550 µL Lysis Buffer (prepared in step 7) into cartridge.
Incubate 20 °C for 2 min, then move front slider to “Beads”.
Do not exceed incubation time; avoid bubbles.
Move side slider to “Retrieval", set timer 30 s, immediately aspirate 5 mL prepared BD Lysis Buffer with P5000M pipette.
After incubation, move side slider to “0", load cartridge with 4 950 µL prepared BD Lysis Buffer.
Remove 5 mL LoBind tube, place on a 5 mL tube magnet, incubate 1 min, remove 4 mL supernatant.
Place cartridge on scanner, start “Retrieval Scan”.
Transfer the remaining 5 mL tube contents (beads + lysis buffer) to a new 1.5 mL LoBind tube, magnet for 2 min, discard supernatant.
Resuspend beads in 1 mL cold Bead Wash Buffer, repeat magnet wash once more.
Keep tube on ice ≤30 min; avoid bubbles.
If beads remain in the 5 mL tube, add 0.5 mL prepared BD Lysis Buffer, resuspend, and transfer.

steps.title: Prepare whole‑transcriptome library
steps.instruction: Generate the WTA library from the retrieved bead‑bound cDNA.

substeps.instruction: Thaw, vortex, and centrifuge all BD Rhapsody WTA Kit reagents; keep on ice.
Dilute purified RPE PCR product with Elution Buffer to 2 nM.
Prepare WTA index PCR mix (per sample, no overage): 25 µL PCR Master Mix, 5 µL nuclease‑free water, 5 µL Library Forward Primer, 5 µL Library Reverse Primer 1‑4 (choose one).
Add 10 µL diluted purified RPE PCR product to the mix, pipet‑mix 10×.
Run PCR: 95 °C 3 min; 8–9 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 60 °C 30 s, 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 1 min; hold 4 °C. Use 9 cycles if concentration <2 nM.
Pause point: store PCR overnight at 4 °C.
Dual‑sided purification:
a. Centrifuge PCR strip, add 60 µL nuclease‑free water to 50 µL product, mix 10×.
b. Transfer 100 µL to new 0.2 mL PCR tube, add 60 µL AMPure beads, mix 10×, incubate 5 min at 20 °C.
c. Magnet 2 min, discard supernatant.
d. Add 15 µL AMPure beads to a new tube, transfer 160 µL supernatant from step b, mix 10×, incubate 5 min.
e. Magnet 1 min, discard supernatant.
f. Add 200 µL 80 % ethanol (on magnet), incubate 30 s, repeat ethanol wash.
g. Remove tube from magnet, briefly centrifuge, keep on magnet, remove residual ethanol, let dry ≤1 min.
h. Resuspend beads in 30 µL Elution Buffer, incubate 20 °C 2 min.
i. Transfer eluate to a new 1.5 mL LoBind tube, label “purified WTA index PCR product”.
j. Store at –20 °C ≤6 months.

steps.title: Prepare optional Sample Tag library
steps.instruction: If Sample Tag labeling was used, generate the Sample Tag library.

substeps.instruction: Dilute Sample Tag PCR2 product with Elution Buffer to 1.1 ng/µL if needed.
Prepare Sample Tag index PCR mix (per sample, no overage): 25 µL PCR Master Mix, 18 µL nuclease‑free water, 2 µL Library Forward Primer, 2 µL Library Reverse Primer 1‑4.
Add 3 µL diluted purified RPE product to reach 50 µL total, pipet‑mix 10×.
Run PCR: 95 °C 3 min; 6–8 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 60 °C 30 s, 72 °C 30 s; final extension 72 °C 1 min; hold 4 °C. Use 6 cycles if concentration <1.1 ng/µL.
Pause point: store PCR overnight at 4 °C.
Purify PCR product:
a. Centrifuge strip, add 40 µL AMPure beads to 50 µL product, mix 10×, incubate 5 min at 20 °C.
b. Magnet 3 min, discard supernatant.
c. Add 200 µL 80 % ethanol (on magnet), incubate 30 s, repeat ethanol wash.
d. Remove tube from magnet, brief centrifugation, keep on magnet, remove residual ethanol, dry 3 min.
e. Resuspend beads in 30 µL Elution Buffer, incubate 20 °C 2 min.
f. Transfer eluate to a new 1.5 mL LoBind tube, label “purified Sample Tag index PCR product”.
g. Store at –20 °C ≤6 months.

steps.title: Quantify and assess library quality
steps.instruction: Measure concentration and size distribution of the purified WTA and optional Sample Tag libraries.

substeps.instruction: Use a Qubit fluorometer (step 65) to measure concentrations; expect >1 ng/µL for WTA and >1.5 ng/µL for Sample Tag.
Run each library on a TapeStation (step 66); WTA index PCR product should show a peak between 250–1000 bp, Sample Tag index PCR product ~270 bp.

steps.title: Import data and set up analysis
steps.instruction: Load raw .h5ad files into Scanpy and prepare for downstream analysis.

substeps.instruction: Import modules: import scanpy as sc, pandas as pd, numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, seaborn as sns.
Read .h5ad file (e.g., file_path = "lung_raw.h5ad"; adata = sc.read_h5ad(file_path)).

steps.title: Perform quality control filtering
steps.instruction: Filter cells based on counts, genes, and mitochondrial content.

substeps.instruction: If multiplexed, keep only desired samples: adata = adata[(adata.obs["Sample_Name"] == "GG") | (adata.obs["Sample_Name"] == "TU")].copy().
Identify mitochondrial genes: adata.var["mt"] = adata.var_names.str.startswith("MT-").
Calculate QC metrics: sc.pp.calculate_qc_metrics(adata, qc_vars=["mt"], log1p=False, inplace=True).
Plot violin of n_genes_by_counts, total_counts, pct_counts_mt to choose thresholds.

Apply filters (example for liver): sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, min_counts=1000); sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, max_counts=100000); sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, min_genes=250); sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, max_genes=8000); adata = adata[adata.obs["pct_counts_mt"] < 30].copy().
Re‑plot violin after filtering to confirm.

steps.title: Normalize and log‑transform data
steps.instruction: Normalize total counts, log‑transform, and store raw counts.

substeps.instruction: Save raw counts: adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.
Normalize: sc.pp.normalize_total(adata).
Log‑transform: sc.pp.log1p(adata).

steps.title: Identify highly variable genes
steps.instruction: Select variable genes using the Seurat v3 method on raw counts.

substeps.instruction: sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, layer="counts", n_top_genes=4000, subset=False, flavor="seurat_v3").

steps.title: Dimensionality reduction and clustering
steps.instruction: Compute PCA, neighbors, UMAP, and Leiden clusters.

substeps.instruction: PCA: sc.tl.pca(adata, mask_var="highly_variable").
Neighbors: sc.pp.neighbors(adata).
UMAP embedding: sc.tl.umap(adata).
Leiden clustering: sc.tl.leiden(adata, resolution=0.5).
Visualize clusters: sc.pl.umap(adata, color="leiden").
Visualize total counts: sc.pl.umap(adata, color="total_counts").

description: The following protocol describes a whole workflow from preparation of single-cell suspensions to primary analysis of single-cell sequencing data (Figure 1). It is optimized to capture cells with low mRNA content (e.g., immune cells such as neutrophils or T cells) obtained from complex human tissues. We utilize the microwell-based BD Rhapsody single-cell sequencing analysis platform, for which significantly better recovery of low-mRNA content cells compared to droplet-based scRNA-seq has recently been demonstrated.1,2 The BD Rhapsody platform comprises several reagent kits, the cartridge kit, the BD Rhapsody Express instrument, and general consumables (see key resources table). We highly recommend using the BD Rhapsody scanner (part of this protocol) as it provides quality control checks during the process of sample preparation and cartridge loading. This enables more precise estimations of cell/bead capture rates, thus allowing optimized sequencing and downstream analysis. The labeling of single cells with universal antibody-oligonucleotides, so-called Sample Tags, is optional and enables the concurrent processing of multiple samples. Additionally, the BD Rhapsody platform also offers simultaneous analysis of mRNA and protein expression by using antigen-specific antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates, so-called AbSeqs (which is not part of this protocol, see3).Figure 1Schematic overview of wet lab workflow As this protocol extends over more than 8 h, stopping points have been incorporated to streamline time management. Overall, we estimate that the complete wet lab processing of the samples will require three full working days. The first three sections provide detailed preparation protocols specific to each tissue type: prostate, lung, and liver. Select the protocol that best suits your specific tissue. From the section “cell counting” onward, the protocol is consistent for all three tissue types.
